title: Headaches at the call center

dispatch.complaint: People are getting headaches by mid-afternoon. It's not hot, just stuffy. The room feels dead.
dispatch.economizer: Honeywell JADE W7220 retrofit, C7232 CO2 sensor for DCV, MS7503 actuator

faults.description: MS7503 actuator dead: good power and signal, no movement.

readings.txt_tstat: Thermostat: occupied, Cool, setpoint 74°F, space 75°F. Y1 and G on.
readings.txt_controller: No unit controller (electromechanical unit). Nothing to report.
readings.txt_look_unit: Unit running normally on mechanical cooling.
readings.txt_look_economizer: OA damper fully shut. Actuator shaft indicator at 0. Coupling tight on the shaft. No sound from the actuator.
readings.txt_manual_stroke: With the actuator released, blades swing open and shut smoothly. No binding.
readings.txt_jade_checkout: DAMPER OPEN: DAMPER OUT goes to 10.0 V. Actuator silent. Blades don't move. DAMPER CLOSE: nothing to close.

hints: What is the JADE asking for vs what the blades are doing?
Before you blame the actuator, prove the damper isn't bound.

diagnosis.label: Economizer actuator failed
diagnosis.feedback: 24.7 VAC power, 5.2 Vdc command, blades free by hand, actuator silent. That's the actuator.

diagnosis.label: Damper/linkage binding
diagnosis.feedback: Blades swing freely by hand. Not binding.

diagnosis.label: JADE output failed
diagnosis.feedback: You measured 5.2 Vdc AT the actuator. The JADE and the wire are fine.

diagnosis.label: CO2 sensor out of calibration
diagnosis.feedback: Your handheld agrees: 1450 ppm. It's real.

diagnosis.label: Minimum position set to zero
diagnosis.feedback: VENTMIN is 3.6 V, and DCV's commanding 5.2 V. The setting's fine.

repair.label: Replace actuator (MS7503-series, match torque & spring-return)
repair.feedback: Damper drives to 40%, CO2 starts dropping within the hour.

repair.label: Lube the linkage and leave
repair.feedback: Linkage was never the problem. Callback.

repair.label: Raise DCV SET to 2000 ppm
repair.feedback: You just told it to ventilate less in a building that's already suffocating.

idealPath.why: DCV ON, DAMPER OUT 5.2 V. JADE is asking for ~40%.
Blades shut. Command and reality disagree.
5.2 Vdc at the actuator. Signal made it.
Lock out before you release the actuator and hand-stroke.
Blades free. That leaves the actuator.

debrief: Power, signal, mechanism: prove each one. 24 VAC in, a real 2-10 Vdc command at the actuator, and blades that move freely by hand leave one suspect. A non-communicating actuator gives the JADE no feedback, so no alarm. Your eyes and meter are the only feedback loop.
